articles.title: Fasting sugar above 126? Here’s why your doctor may still not diagnose diabetes
articles.description: A fasting blood sugar reading above 126 mg/dL can be concerning, but it doesn’t confirm diabetes on its own, explains Dr Pranav Ghody. Diagnosis requires consistent results and supporting tests like HbA1c or an oral glucose tolerance test, as blood sugar levels can fluctuate due to factors like stress, poor sleep, illness, medications, or even recent meals. Lab variations may also affect readings, which is why repeat testing is recommended. In some cases, individuals may have prediabetes rather than diabetes, and doctors also consider symptoms, medical history, and overall risk before making a diagnosis—focusing on patterns over time rather than a single value.
